cards.title: For o since
cards.summary: Con el presente perfecto, for indica cuánto tiempo dura algo y since indica cuándo empezó.
cards.form: for + período (for two years) · since + momento de inicio (since 2020)
uses: For: un período de tiempo (for three days, for a long time).
Since: el momento en que empezó (since May, since I was a child).
Los dos se usan sobre todo con el presente perfecto: I have lived here for… / since…

pitfalls.wrong: I live here since 2019.
pitfalls.why: Para algo que empezó en el pasado y sigue ahora se usa el presente perfecto, no el presente.

pitfalls.wrong: I have worked here since three years.
pitfalls.right: I have worked here for three years.
pitfalls.why: Con un período (three years) se usa for; since va con el momento de inicio.

pitfalls.wrong: She has been sick during two days.
pitfalls.right: She has been sick for two days.
pitfalls.why: Para decir cuánto dura algo se usa for, no during.

examples.en: I have lived in this city for ten years.
examples.es: Vivo en esta ciudad desde hace diez años.

examples.en: We have known each other since high school.
examples.es: Nos conocemos desde la secundaria.

examples.es: Están casados desde hace mucho tiempo.

examples.en: He has had that car for six months.

cards.title: Say o tell
cards.summary: Las dos significan «decir». Tell casi siempre lleva a quién se lo dices (tell me); say no lo necesita.
cards.form: say + algo (+ to + persona) · tell + persona + algo
uses: Say: repetir palabras o decir algo sin nombrar a la persona (She said hello).
Tell + persona: He told me the truth.
Expresiones fijas con tell: tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke.

pitfalls.wrong: She said me that she was tired.
pitfalls.right: She told me that she was tired.
pitfalls.why: Si la persona va justo después del verbo, se usa tell, no say.

pitfalls.wrong: He told that he was busy.
pitfalls.right: He said that he was busy.
pitfalls.why: Tell necesita a quién (told me, told us). Sin persona, usa say.

pitfalls.wrong: Can you say me the time?
pitfalls.right: Can you tell me the time?
pitfalls.why: «Decirme» algo a mí es tell me.

pitfalls.wrong: Don't say lies.
pitfalls.why: En inglés se dice tell a lie y tell the truth.

examples.es: Dijo que estaba cansada.

cards.title: Too y enough
cards.summary: Too significa «demasiado» y va antes del adjetivo. Enough significa «suficiente»: va después del adjetivo y antes del sustantivo.
cards.form: too + adjetivo · adjetivo + enough · enough + sustantivo
uses: Too: más de lo necesario (too expensive, too late).
Adjetivo + enough: lo necesario (old enough, warm enough).
Enough + sustantivo: enough money, enough time.
Not … enough: falta algo (not big enough).

pitfalls.wrong: This coffee is enough hot.
pitfalls.why: Con adjetivos, enough va después: hot enough.

pitfalls.wrong: I don't have money enough.
pitfalls.why: Con sustantivos, enough va antes: enough money.

pitfalls.wrong: The movie was too much long.
pitfalls.why: Antes de un adjetivo se usa solo too, sin much.

pitfalls.wrong: It's very cold to swim.
pitfalls.why: Para decir que algo impide hacer otra cosa se usa too, no very.

examples.en: This bag is too heavy for me.
examples.es: Esta bolsa es demasiado pesada para mí.

examples.en: He isn't old enough to drive.
examples.es: No tiene edad suficiente para manejar.

cards.title: Much, many y a lot of
cards.summary: Las tres expresan cantidad. Many va con sustantivos contables, much con incontables y a lot of con los dos.
cards.form: many + plural · much + incontable · a lot of + los dos
uses: Many: cosas que se cuentan (many friends, many books).
Much: cosas que no se cuentan (much time, much money), sobre todo en negativas y preguntas.
A lot of: con los dos, sobre todo en oraciones afirmativas (a lot of people, a lot of water).
How many / how much para preguntar cantidades.

pitfalls.wrong: I don't have many money.
pitfalls.why: Money es incontable: se usa much.

pitfalls.wrong: There are much people here.
pitfalls.right: There are a lot of people here.
pitfalls.why: People es plural: many o a lot of, nunca much.

pitfalls.wrong: How much brothers do you have?
pitfalls.right: How many brothers do you have?
pitfalls.why: Para cosas que se cuentan se pregunta how many.

pitfalls.wrong: I have a lot of works.
pitfalls.right: I have a lot of work.
pitfalls.why: Work (trabajo) es incontable: no lleva -s.

cards.title: Presente simple para rutinas
cards.summary: Sirve para hablar de lo que haces habitualmente. Con he, she e it, el verbo afirmativo lleva -s o -es.
cards.form: I / you / we / they + verbo · he / she / it + verbo-s · don't / doesn't + verbo
uses: Rutinas y hábitos: I get up at seven every day.
Con he, she, it el verbo suma -s (works, gets) o -es (watches, goes); have pasa a has.
Negativas y preguntas con do / does: She doesn't work on Sundays. Does he cook?
Suele ir con usually, always, never y every day.

pitfalls.wrong: She get up at seven.
pitfalls.why: Con he, she o it el verbo afirmativo lleva -s.

pitfalls.wrong: He don't work on Sundays.
pitfalls.why: Con he, she o it la negativa es doesn't.

pitfalls.wrong: Does she works here?
pitfalls.why: Después de does el verbo va sin -s.

pitfalls.wrong: I am get up at six every day.
pitfalls.right: I get up at six every day.
pitfalls.why: Para rutinas no se agrega am, is o are delante del verbo.

cards.title: There is y there are
cards.summary: Equivalen a «hay». There is va con un sustantivo singular o incontable y there are, con un plural.
cards.form: there is + singular / incontable · there are + plural · is there…? / are there…?
uses: Decir qué hay en un lugar: There is a sofa in the living room.
Con plurales: There are two bedrooms.
Negativas: there isn't / there aren't (any).
Preguntas: Is there a bathroom? Are there any windows?

pitfalls.wrong: Have two bedrooms in my house.
pitfalls.right: There are two bedrooms in my house.
pitfalls.why: «Hay» no se dice con have: se usa there is o there are.

pitfalls.wrong: There is three chairs in the kitchen.
pitfalls.right: There are three chairs in the kitchen.
pitfalls.why: Con un plural se usa there are.

pitfalls.wrong: Is a park near your house?
pitfalls.right: Is there a park near your house?
pitfalls.why: En la pregunta no se puede omitir there.

pitfalls.wrong: It is a big window in my bedroom.
pitfalls.right: There is a big window in my bedroom.
pitfalls.why: Para decir que algo existe en un lugar se usa there is, no it is.

cards.title: Should para dar consejos
cards.summary: Should + verbo sirve para dar o pedir consejos. Equivale a «deberías» o «debería».
cards.form: should / shouldn't + verbo base · should I…?
uses: Dar un consejo: You should see a doctor.
Aconsejar que no se haga algo: You shouldn't go to work today.
Pedir consejo: What should I do? Should I take this medicine?
Es igual para todas las personas: he should, she should (sin -s).

pitfalls.wrong: You should to rest.
pitfalls.why: Después de should va el verbo sin to.

pitfalls.wrong: She shoulds go to bed early.
pitfalls.right: She should go to bed early.
pitfalls.why: Should no cambia con he, she o it.

pitfalls.wrong: You don't should go to work.
pitfalls.why: La negativa es shouldn't (should not), sin don't.

pitfalls.wrong: Do I should take this medicine?
pitfalls.why: En preguntas, should va antes del sujeto, sin do.

cards.title: Have to y don't have to
cards.summary: Have to + verbo expresa una obligación: «tener que». Don't have to significa que algo no es necesario.
cards.form: have to / has to + verbo base · don't / doesn't have to + verbo base · do you have to…?
uses: Obligaciones: I have to work on Saturdays.
Con he, she, it se usa has to: She has to get up early.
Algo que no es necesario: You don't have to come (no hace falta que vengas).
Preguntas con do / does: Do you have to work tomorrow?

pitfalls.why: Después de have to va el verbo base.

pitfalls.wrong: She have to finish this today.

pitfalls.wrong: You haven't to come.
pitfalls.why: La negativa se forma con don't o doesn't: don't have to.

pitfalls.wrong: He doesn't has to cook.
pitfalls.why: Después de doesn't, has vuelve a have.

cards.title: Comparativos: older than, more interesting than
cards.summary: Para comparar dos personas o cosas: adjetivo corto + -er + than, o more + adjetivo largo + than.
cards.form: adjetivo corto + -er + than · more + adjetivo largo + than · good → better, bad → worse
uses: Adjetivos cortos: old → older, tall → taller, big → bigger.
Terminados en -y: happy → happier, funny → funnier.
Adjetivos largos: more interesting, more expensive.
Irregulares: good → better, bad → worse.

pitfalls.wrong: My brother is more tall than me.
pitfalls.right: My brother is taller than me.
pitfalls.why: Con adjetivos cortos se agrega -er; no se usa more.

pitfalls.wrong: She is older that her sister.
pitfalls.right: She is older than her sister.
pitfalls.why: El «que» de una comparación es than, no that.

pitfalls.wrong: This book is more good than that one.
pitfalls.right: This book is better than that one.
pitfalls.why: Good es irregular: better.

pitfalls.wrong: My aunt is more younger than my mom.
pitfalls.right: My aunt is younger than my mom.
pitfalls.why: No se usan more y -er al mismo tiempo.

cards.title: Some, any y I would like
cards.summary: Some y any significan «algo de» o «unos». Some va en afirmativas, ofrecimientos y pedidos; any, en negativas y preguntas. I would like… es la forma educada de pedir.
cards.form: some + plural / incontable · any en negativas y preguntas · I would like (I'd like) + sustantivo / to + verbo
uses: Some en afirmativas: I bought some bread.
Any en negativas y preguntas: We don't have any milk. Do you have any eggs?
Some en ofrecimientos y pedidos: Would you like some coffee? Can I have some water?
I'd like para pedir con cortesía: I'd like a chicken sandwich, please.

pitfalls.wrong: We don't have some rice.
pitfalls.why: En negativas se usa any.

pitfalls.wrong: I would like order the chicken.
pitfalls.right: I would like to order the chicken.
pitfalls.why: Delante de un verbo, would like lleva to.

pitfalls.wrong: I like a glass of water, please.
pitfalls.right: I would like a glass of water, please.
pitfalls.why: Para pedir algo se usa would like (I'd like); I like significa «me gusta».

pitfalls.wrong: There isn't any breads.
pitfalls.why: Bread es incontable: no lleva -s.

examples.en: I'd like a chicken sandwich, please.
examples.es: Quisiera un sándwich de pollo, por favor.

examples.en: We need some vegetables for dinner.
examples.es: Necesitamos verduras para la cena.

examples.en: We don't have any rice.
examples.es: No tenemos arroz.

examples.en: Do you have any bread?
examples.es: ¿Tienes pan?

examples.en: Would you like some coffee?
examples.es: ¿Quieres un poco de café?

examples.en: I would like to order now.

cards.title: Can para habilidades
cards.summary: Can + verbo dice lo que alguien sabe o puede hacer. Es igual para todas las personas y la negativa es can't.
cards.form: can / can't + verbo base · can you…? · could (pasado)
uses: Habilidades: I can swim. She can play the guitar.
Lo que no sabes hacer: I can't dance.
Preguntas y respuestas cortas: Can you cook? — Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
En pasado: could / couldn't (I could swim when I was five).

pitfalls.wrong: I can to swim.
pitfalls.why: Después de can va el verbo sin to.

pitfalls.wrong: She cans play the piano.
pitfalls.why: Can no lleva -s con he, she o it.

pitfalls.wrong: Do you can speak English?
pitfalls.why: En preguntas, can va antes del sujeto, sin do.

pitfalls.wrong: I don't can dance.
pitfalls.why: La negativa es can't (cannot), sin don't.

examples.en: I can play the guitar.
examples.es: Sé tocar la guitarra.

examples.en: My little brother can't swim yet.
examples.es: Mi hermano menor todavía no sabe nadar.

examples.en: Can you cook?
examples.es: ¿Sabes cocinar?

examples.en: She can run very fast.
examples.es: Ella puede correr muy rápido.

examples.en: He can speak three languages.
examples.es: Él habla tres idiomas.

examples.en: I could swim when I was five.
examples.es: Sabía nadar cuando tenía cinco años.

cards.title: On, in y at con el tiempo
cards.summary: On va con días y fechas; in, con meses, años y partes del día; at, con horas.
cards.form: on + día / fecha · in + mes / año / estación / parte del día · at + hora
uses: On: días y fechas (on Monday, on May 12, on my birthday).
In: meses, años, estaciones y partes del día (in July, in 2020, in summer, in the morning).
At: horas y momentos exactos (at nine o'clock, at noon, at night).
Sin preposición con every, next, last y this: I work every Monday.

pitfalls.wrong: I have a meeting in Monday.
pitfalls.right: I have a meeting on Monday.
pitfalls.why: Con los días de la semana se usa on.

pitfalls.wrong: The class starts in nine o'clock.
pitfalls.right: The class starts at nine o'clock.
pitfalls.why: Con horas se usa at.

pitfalls.wrong: My birthday is on July.
pitfalls.why: Con meses (sin día) se usa in.

pitfalls.wrong: See you on next Friday.
pitfalls.why: Con next, last, this y every no se usa preposición.

examples.en: I don't work on Sundays.
examples.es: No trabajo los domingos.

examples.en: The meeting is at ten o'clock.
examples.es: La reunión es a las diez.

examples.en: We go on vacation in August.
examples.es: Nos vamos de vacaciones en agosto.

examples.en: I study in the morning and work in the afternoon.
examples.es: Estudio por la mañana y trabajo por la tarde.

examples.en: My birthday is on May 12.
examples.es: Mi cumpleaños es el 12 de mayo.

examples.en: She finishes work at five on Fridays.
examples.es: Ella termina de trabajar a las cinco los viernes.

cards.title: Going to para predicciones
cards.summary: Be going to + verbo sirve para decir lo que va a pasar cuando ya se ve venir, como «va a llover».
cards.form: am / is / are + going to + verbo base
uses: Predicciones con pruebas: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
El clima de los próximos días: It's going to be cold tonight.
Negativas: It isn't going to snow.
Preguntas: Is it going to rain tomorrow?

pitfalls.wrong: It going to rain.
pitfalls.why: Falta el verbo be: it is (it's) going to.

pitfalls.wrong: It's going to raining.
pitfalls.why: Después de going to va el verbo base.

pitfalls.wrong: Is going to be sunny tomorrow.
pitfalls.right: It's going to be sunny tomorrow.
pitfalls.why: En inglés el sujeto es obligatorio: para el clima se usa it.

pitfalls.wrong: Look at the sky! It rains soon.
pitfalls.right: Look at the sky! It's going to rain soon.
pitfalls.why: Para predecir algo que ves venir se usa going to, no el presente.

examples.en: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
examples.es: Mira esas nubes. Va a llover.

examples.en: Take an umbrella. It's going to rain this afternoon.
examples.es: Lleva un paraguas. Va a llover esta tarde.

examples.en: It's going to be very hot tomorrow.
examples.es: Mañana va a hacer mucho calor.

examples.en: It isn't going to snow this week.
examples.es: No va a nevar esta semana.

examples.en: Is it going to be sunny on Saturday?
examples.es: ¿Va a hacer sol el sábado?

examples.en: You're going to be cold in that shirt.
examples.es: Vas a tener frío con esa camisa.
